grades.quote: PLV0 is the privilege level with the highest privilege and is the only privilege level that can use privileged instructions and access all privileged resources.
grades.reason: Gives general background on the PLV0–PLV3 privilege levels in LoongArch, which is needed to interpret RPLV. It never mentions RPLV or TLB entry checks.
This is only a table-of-contents fragment. It has no information about RPLV or privilege checks.

grades.quote: When RPLV=0, the page table entry can be accessed by any program whose privilege level is not lower than PLV; when RPLV=1, the page table entry can only be accessed by programs whose privilege level is equal to PLV.
grades.reason: This is the TLBELO0/TLBELO1 field table. The first table has 64-bit fields (NR, NX, RPLV at bits 61–63), so it is the LA64 definition. It says directly how RPLV changes access to the entry: with RPLV=0, any privilege level not lower than PLV may access it, and with RPLV=1, only the level equal to PLV may.

grades.quote: When RPLV=0, the page table entry can be accessed by any program whose privilege level is not lower than PLV; when RPLV=1, the page table entry can only be accessed by programs whose privilege level is equal to PLV.
grades.reason: This is the LA64 TLBRELO0/TLBRELO1 (TLB refill exception) register table. It gives the same RPLV semantics. The context is the refill-exception copy of the entry rather than the main TLB entry register, so it is slightly less direct.
